"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/bulb-switcher/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

319. Bulb Switcher

There are n bulbs that are initially off. You first turn on all the bulbs, then you turn off every second bulb.

On the third round, you toggle every third bulb (turning on if it's off or turning off if it's on). For the ith round, you toggle every i bulb. For the nth round, you only toggle the last bulb.

Return the number of bulbs that are on after n rounds.

Example 1:

Input: n = 3
Output: 1
Explanation: At first, the three bulbs are [off, off, off].
After the first round, the three bulbs are [on, on, on].
After the second round, the three bulbs are [on, off, on].
After the third round, the three bulbs are [on, off, off].
So you should return 1 because there is only one bulb is on.

Example 2:

Input: n = 0
Output: 0

Example 3:

Input: n = 1
Output: 1

Constraints:

    0 <= n <= 10^9
"""


class Solution:
    def bulbSwitch(self, n: int) -> int:
        # The bulbs that remain on are those toggled an odd number of times,
        # which happens only for bulbs at positions that are perfect squares.
        # So the answer is the count of perfect squares <= n, which is floor(sqrt(n)).
        return int(sqrt(n))


sol = Solution()

print(sol.bulbSwitch(3))  # 1

assert sol.bulbSwitch(3) == 1
assert sol.bulbSwitch(0) == 0
assert sol.bulbSwitch(1) == 1

assert sol.bulbSwitch(10) == 3
assert sol.bulbSwitch(16) == 4
assert sol.bulbSwitch(25) == 5
assert sol.bulbSwitch(26) == 5
assert sol.bulbSwitch(100) == 10
assert sol.bulbSwitch(999999999) == 31622
assert sol.bulbSwitch(1000000000) == 31622
assert sol.bulbSwitch(2) == 1
assert sol.bulbSwitch(4) == 2
assert sol.bulbSwitch(5) == 2
assert sol.bulbSwitch(15) == 3
assert sol.bulbSwitch(2147395600) == 46340
